history.heading: Province of Freedom
paragraphs: Sierra Leone, on the West African coast, was home to the Temne, Mende, Limba and other peoples. Portuguese navigator Pedro de Sintra named its mountains Serra Leoa ("Lion Mountains") in 1462. Bunce Island became a major British slave-trading fort.

In 1787 British abolitionists founded a settlement for freed slaves, including Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia and Jamaican Maroons, which became Freetown. It became a British colony in 1808 and a base for the Royal Navy's campaign against the slave trade; tens of thousands of liberated Africans were resettled there. Their descendants formed the Krio community.

history.heading: Independence and civil war
paragraphs: Sierra Leone became independent on 27 April 1961. Coups and one-party rule under Siaka Stevens followed. A brutal civil war from 1991 to 2002, fuelled by "blood diamonds", killed about 50,000 people; the Revolutionary United Front became infamous for amputations and child soldiers. British and UN intervention helped end the war.
A UN-backed Special Court convicted war criminals, including Liberia's Charles Taylor. The 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic killed nearly 4,000 people in Sierra Leone.

culture.heading: Peoples and traditions
paragraphs: English is official, and Krio, an English-based creole, is the common language. The Mende and Temne are the largest groups. About three-quarters of people are Muslim and most others Christian, with notable religious tolerance and intermarriage.
Secret societies such as Poro and Bondo play roles in initiation. Cassava leaf stew and groundnut soup are popular. Football is the most popular sport.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: Sierra Leone is a presidential republic with two main parties, the Sierra Leone People's Party and the All People's Congress, with regional support bases. President Julius Maada Bio was re-elected in 2023 in a disputed vote, and an attempted coup was foiled later that year.

economy.heading: Mining and agriculture
paragraphs: Sierra Leone is rich in diamonds, iron ore, rutile, bauxite and gold, but remains one of the poorest countries in the world. Most people depend on subsistence farming, especially rice and cassava. The currency is the leone, redenominated in 2022.
